messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@livecart.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 28 Sep 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Evaluating hosted for LiveCart — scope, endpoint mapping, and rate profile

Hi Hannah — thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap from my side and a few open questions we need to lock down before we sign up for a pilot:

- Use case: customer support summarization + live answer generation in our web console (low-latency chat).
- Traffic profile (approx): baseline ~20 requests/sec during business hours, peaks up to 80 req/s for short bursts (2–5 minutes), average msg length ~120 tokens, occasional long summaries ~1,200 tokens.
- Latency target: p95 inference < 300ms for the short responses (we can tolerate 800ms for long summaries).
- Data residency: US-only required.
- Compliance: standard security questionnaire in progress; no on-prem requirement yet but may be considered if we go enterprise.

Questions we want clarity on for Hosted evaluation:
1) Quickstart: how fast can we get sandbox endpoints and what constraints are applied (rate limits, token caps)?
2) Endpoint mapping: can we create separate endpoints per flow (chat, summarization) with different rate caps and models?
3) Burst behavior: how are short bursts handled on Hosted — is there a burst pool or throttling?
4) Prefetch / prefix caching: what are recommended configs for chat contexts to reduce token cost and latency?
5) Cost signal: early estimate for a 30-day pilot (slice of capacity) so we can budget internally.

I've attached a CSV with a sampled hour of traffic (file: livecart_traffic_sample.csv) — will upload the full day if useful. Alicia (cc'd) will be our technical lead on this.

Prefer a short follow-up call next week (30 minutes) to go over sandbox access and the pilot proposal.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Head of Platform
LiveCart
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Evaluating hosted for LiveCart — scope, endpoint mapping, and rate profile

Sanjay — great to meet you and Alicia today. Short answers and proposed next steps below. I also captured internal owners so we can move quickly.

Recap + quick answers:
- Sandbox quickstart: we can provision sandbox endpoints within 48 hours. Default sandbox caps are conservative (see below) but we can request a pilot slice after reviewing traffic.
- Endpoint mapping: yes — you can create multiple endpoints (e.g., chat, summarizer) and assign different model/config profiles and rate caps per endpoint.
- Burst behavior: Hosted uses a rate-slicing model. For pilots we typically give a guaranteed baseline slice plus a controlled burst allowance; sustained higher throughput is routed to Dedicated.
- Prefetch/prefix caching: for chat we recommend prefix (system + initial context) caching at the endpoint level plus KV caching for per-user recent context — this cuts token re-generation and latency for repeat patterns.

Numbers (sandbox defaults, examples):
- Default sandbox endpoint: 50 requests/minute, 5 concurrent requests, soft token cap 60k tokens/min.
- Pilot slice (request-based): e.g., baseline 30 req/s (concurrency 10) + 3x short burst allowance for 5-minute windows.
- Production Hosted typical baseline where Dedicated becomes recommended: sustained >200 req/s or strict p95 < 200ms SLO.

Next steps I propose:
1) You send the full 24-hour traffic CSV (we'll use it to size a pilot slice and caching config).
2) I loop in Ben Carter (solutions) to produce endpoint mapping + sandbox rate slice proposal and a 30-day pilot estimate.
3) Sign NDA (we can send a basic mutual NDA within 24 hours) and provision sandbox access.
4) Short follow-up call (30 min) — Ben + Priya (rev ops) join to confirm contract/pilot terms.

Attaching a short checklist and a stub pilot request form. If these sandbox caps are too low for your initial tests we'll escalate to a larger slice but want to size it to your observed traffic first.

Available times for the follow-up: Mon 10/2 9–11am PT, Tue 10/3 1–4pm PT. Which works for you?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
